summary: Wake County tower, about 99 ft, erected 1937 on Six Forks Road; moved to Howard Road in 1968; last manned 1985; vacant, still standing.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower of about 99 feet, per the forestry history; WRAL reports a 20-foot increase at the move
facts.status_note: WRAL (posted 2023-05-17) calls the Howard Road tower vacant; the forestry history (last updated 2017) says it is no longer used; an undated Legeros blog says it is still standing. No source describes the 1937 Six Forks Road site today.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The forestry history gives about 99 feet for both the 1937 tower and the 1968 re-erection. WRAL quotes Jerry Tilley saying 20 feet was added when the tower moved. The sources do not resolve this.

notes_for_editor: The Legeros forestry page is marked 'Last updated: January 28, 2017' and the WRAL article is posted 2023-05-17. The Legeros blog has no visible date in the cached copy, so its 'still standing' is undated. The story dates 'vacant' and 'no longer used' to those sources. The forestry history says the ranger house is a private residence, while WRAL says it is now the NC Forest Service office; the story does not resolve this.The statewide list has a second record, Bayleaf (Raleigh) at 35.88916, -78.68333, which may be the Howard Road tower; the 'old' coordinates were not checked against the 1936 Six Forks Road site, and the record was not changed. Height conflict is in resolved_conflicts. No photos added.
